supporting_observations.claim: WS-MFISCHER-01 repeatedly issued proxy CONNECT requests to update.ledgerlink.co:443 from 13:35:49 through 14:05:49 UTC, at roughly five-minute intervals. The proxy records include both successful tunnels and errors.

The requests are associated with ledgerlinkupd.exe running as PID 4016 from max.fischer's AppData\Local\LedgerLink directory, rather than the approved inventory path under C:\Program Files\LedgerLink.

The observed hostname ends in ledgerlink.co, while the supplied inventory lists update.ledgerlink.com as the approved LedgerLink updater endpoint. The hostname and executable-path differences warrant investigation, but do not alone establish maliciousness.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT destinations, status, and tunnel byte counts, but the available logs do not reveal the encrypted HTTPS contents or what, if anything, was downloaded.
The available records do not establish the executable's hash, signature, installation source, or whether the AppData copy is an authorized LedgerLink version.
The supplied evidence shows no proxy CONNECT to update.ledgerlink.co after 14:05:49 UTC in the review window; it therefore does not establish an exact 14:10 connection.
claims_not_established: Whether update.ledgerlink.co is an authorized alternate endpoint or a lookalike used by an unauthorized updater.
Whether ledgerlinkupd.exe is genuine, modified, or malicious.
Whether any successful tunnel delivered executable content or resulted in compromise.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and verify the hash, digital signature, version, and provenance of C:\Users\max.fischer\AppData\Local\LedgerLink\ledgerlinkupd.exe; compare it with an approved LedgerLink installer or known-good endpoint.
Confirm with the LedgerLink owner or vendor whether update.ledgerlink.co is authorized, and verify the destination using DNS, certificate, and proxy/TLS inspection records if available.
Review endpoint file, download, and process telemetry around the updater's launch and exit to determine whether it wrote or executed additional content.
unrelated_findings: DropboxUpdate.exe ran as SYSTEM on WS-MFISCHER-01. Dropbox is not among the approved software or services in the supplied inventory; review separately. The available records here show process start and exit, not network activity. (T235-00250, T235-00251, T235-00257, T235-00258)
